title: SnapKV: LLM Knows What You are Looking for Before Generation
technique: fine-tuning-free prompt KV compression: select clustered important KV positions per head using an observation window at the end of the prompt

optimized_metrics.evidence: SnapKV, an innovative and fine-tuning-free approach that efficiently minimizes KV cache size while still delivering comparable performance in real-world applications
SnapKV achieves a consistent decoding speed with a 3.6x increase in generation speed and an 8.2x enhancement in memory efficiency compared to the baseline when processing inputs of 16K tokens
it maintains comparable performance to the baseline models across 16 long sequence datasets

headline_claim.text: SnapKV achieves a consistent decoding speed with a 3.6x increase in generation speed and an 8.2x enhancement in memory efficiency compared to the baseline when processing inputs of 16K tokens.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 7 decode latency ms/token vs input length
Fig 7 max input before OOM; 380K on one A100

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The x-axis denotes the input sequence length; the y-axis indicates decoding latency (ms/token).
metric_definitions.notes: per-step decode latency at batch sizes 1-4 (HF implementation); no TTFT/prefill timing

metric_definitions.definition_quote: at a batch size of 2, the baseline model encounters an OOM error beyond 16k input tokens, whereas the SnapKV-enhanced model extends this limit to 131k input tokens, indicating an approximately 8.2x improvement.
metric_definitions.notes: memory efficiency = max feasible input length before OOM, not bytes

load_regime: batch-size and input-length sweep (fixed generation length 512, max KV cache 2048); no request arrivals
tradeoff_acknowledged: negligible accuracy drop in Needle-in-a-Haystack; prompt-only compression
extractor_notes: Latency here is per-token decode speed (batch-level decode time), not serving TPOT under load. Core objective is KV size reduction with accuracy preserved; speed and memory gains are consequences.
